h1: Fluidstack ARR: ~$660M From GPU Tenant-Operator to Google's TPU Landlord.

modelTitle: How Renting TPU Shells Yields $25M Per Megawatt.
modelParagraphs: Fluidstack is a tenant-operator: it leases data center shells, fills them with accelerators — mostly Google TPUs — and rents the capacity to AI labs under multi-year contracts. Early deals averaged around $340K; by 2025 new contracts were being signed at $20-25M of revenue per MW of IT capacity, which is how a $180M ARR business projected ~$660M for 2026 once the large sites landed.

The company's leverage is its relationship stack. Google backstops Fluidstack's data center leases — agreeing to take over payments if Fluidstack defaults — which underpins roughly $35B in TPU chip deals tied to Anthropic. Anthropic itself committed $50B to US data centers built with Fluidstack in Texas and New York. A $1.5B round led by Jane Street in September 2026 valued the company at $18B, up from roughly $10B earlier in the year.

faqs.a: Fluidstack's 2026 projected revenue is roughly $660 million, per figures reported to investors, up from $180M of ARR in 2024. The figure is a projection driven by contracted data center capacity, classified here as Reported.

faqs.q: How Did Fluidstack Grow From $180M to ~$660M?
faqs.a: Contract size. Early deals averaged ~$340K; by 2025 Fluidstack was signing multi-year contracts at $20-25M of revenue per MW. The inflection was Anthropic's November 2025 announcement of a $50B US data center program built with Fluidstack in Texas and New York.

faqs.q: What Is Fluidstack's Relationship With Google?
faqs.a: Fluidstack is the first known operator of Google TPU capacity outside Google, effectively a test bed for Google selling its AI chips as an NVIDIA alternative. Google also backstops Fluidstack's data center leases — taking over payments if Fluidstack defaults — underpinning ~$35B in TPU deals tied to Anthropic.
A $1.5 billion round led by Jane Street in September 2026 valued Fluidstack at $18 billion, up from marks around $10B earlier in 2026 that had been secured by GPU assets.

Anthropic is the anchor — the $50B Texas and New York build-out — alongside other AI labs renting contracted capacity. Google is the strategic counterparty on the TPU side, backstopping leases tied to roughly $35B of chip deals.
